title: Ownership Practices & Smells
body:
# Ownership Practices & Code Smells

## Borrow before cloning

```rust
// BAD: full heap copy just to read
fn count_vowels(s: String) -> usize { /* … */ }

// GOOD: borrow, no allocation
fn count_vowels(s: &str) -> usize { /* … */ }
```

Every `.clone()` is a decision to pay for memory + time. Make it deliberate:
clone at API boundaries when ownership is genuinely required, not to appease
the checker without reading its message.

## Understand, don't fight, the borrow checker

When an error appears, ask *which rule* fired (single writer? lifetime?). The
fix is usually restructuring — e.g. ending a scope early — rather than wrapping
everything in smart pointers.

## Avoid premature Rc/Arc

```rust
// BAD: reference-counting to dodge a design question
struct Ctx { data: Rc<Config> }
```

Shared ownership adds runtime cost and hides data flow. Prefer passing `&`
references down; reach for `Rc`/`Arc` when ownership graphs genuinely fork
(GUI trees, task-shared caches).

## Smell: unnecessary reference nesting

`&&&String` almost never helps — auto-deref makes one level enough. If you see
double refs, simplify the signature.

## Smell: needless lifetime parameters

Adding `'a` where elision already works is noise. Let inference win; annotate
only what the compiler asks for.
